note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: NIO absorbed a RMB 10,000/vehicle purchase-tax subsidy on ES8 orders locked through 30 April 2026 and then discontinued it mid-Q2 — Deutsche Bank named that discontinuation as a cause of the June ES8 order shortfall. ES8 (Gen 3) was 33,474 units of Q2's 107,658, so removing RMB 10,000/unit from even ~18,000 Q2 deliveries retains ~RMB 180m of margin, which is the whole of Deutsche Bank's ~RMB 180m Q2 non-GAAP net income estimate. The 2.1% unit miss versus the 110-115k guide was in part the price paid for that margin, not purely demand weakness.
findings.adversary_note: Every factual component of this claim is in English-language, US-retail-facing wire copy and has been since 2 July 2026. CnEVPost (2026-07-02) reports Deutsche Bank's Wang Bin attributing the June ES8 order decline to the phase-out of the RMB 10,000 purchase-tax subsidy plus customers waiting for the five-seat variant, and that DB still expected non-GAAP breakeven in Q2. That exact note was syndicated to Stocktwits, TradingView, MSN and Asianet under the headline 'Deutsche Bank Sees ES8 Drag, But Q2 Breakeven Still In Play' -- i.e. the subsidy withdrawal AND the margin-supportive conclusion were published together. DB's ~RMB 180m Q2 non-GAAP net income estimate is in the hunter's own other source, CnEVPost 2026-08-20. The only unpublished element is the hunter's arithmetic, and that arithmetic is timing-wrong: the subsidy applied to orders locked through end-April/May, so the great majority of Q2 ES8 deliveries CARRIED the cost; withdrawing it in June saves money on June-locked orders whose deliveries land mostly in Q3, not Q2. So the RMB 180m is not 'retained in Q2'. Note also that the July DB note put non-GAAP net profit at RMB 5m, and the August note at RMB 180m -- the 180m coincidence the hunter leans on is two numbers from different vintages, not one identity. Residual value: consensus is a $0.05/ADS loss while DB is at breakeven-to-positive, so a real non-GAAP profit print is still a live spread, which is why this is 78 and not 92.

findings.finding: NIO's 20-F for FY2025, filed 2026-04-10, discloses that headcount fell to 35,032 from 45,635 — 10,603 jobs, the sharpest single-year cut in its history — with product and software development down 40% to 6,912 from 11,528 and 'user experience' (sales, marketing, service) down 30.8% to 16,885 from 24,410. NIO never gave aggregate numbers during 2025, calling it 'organizational optimization'. Q2 2026 volume was +29% sequentially (107,658 vs 83,465) against that reduced cost base.
findings.adversary_note: This was filed 2026-04-10 and covered in English within 48 hours, including on Yahoo Finance. Simply Wall St via Yahoo (2026-04-12) states NIO 'announced its sharpest workforce reduction to date for 2025, cutting 10,600 jobs' with 'a 40% reduction in research and development staff' and explicitly draws the operating-leverage inference: 'a clear shift in focus toward getting more vehicles out the door while keeping an eye on costs.' eletric-vehicles.com ran an 1,800-word piece under the headline 'Nio Discloses 10,600 Job Cuts in 2025, With 40% of R&D Staff Eliminated', and the 35,032 figure has propagated to macrotrends and stockanalysis.com as a data field. More decisively, the mechanism does not need the 20-F at all: the reduced cost base has already shown up in two reported quarters since the cut -- Q4 2025 delivered NIO's first GAAP quarterly net profit (RMB 282.7m) and Q1 2026 an 18.8% vehicle margin with positive non-GAAP operating income, both widely reported. The market has already observed the operating leverage in actual financials; the headcount table is the explanation, not new news. The claim's sub-figures do check out arithmetically (11,528->6,912 = -40.0%; 24,410->16,885 = -30.8%), so this is not wrong -- just old and consumed.

findings.finding: NIO's year-on-year growth rate collapses mechanically from the August number onward on base effects, and 1 September is NIO's established monthly-delivery publication slot, so the August figure plausibly lands in the same tape as Q2 results and the Q3 guide. July 2026 was 35,934, +71.0% YoY against a July 2025 base of ~21,017. But August 2025 was 31,305 and September 2025 was 34,749 (Q3 2025 total 87,071) — the base steps up ~49% in one month. Bottom-up August 2026 indicators point to roughly flat-to-modestly-up sequentially (third-gen ES8's latest 10,000 units took 30 days as of 21 August; Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days), implying Q3 near 113-118k and YoY growth roughly halving to ~+30%.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves are published, and the second half is published in the hunter's own other source. (a) The 'compound catalyst' is explicit in CnEVPost 2026-08-20: 'Management will hold an earnings call at 8 a.m. New York time on September 1, the same date Nio is due to publish its August deliveries' -- the same article cited for NIO-h1#4 -- and it has been repeated across the English preview corpus (TipRanks, Blockonomi, MoneyCheck, eletric-vehicles, Electric Viking). Eleven days of notice on a name with 27m ADS/day. The chain agrees it is pricing more than one event: a 10.18% straddle over four calendar days at 104.5% ATM IV, with a legible bid and only 7% of mid in spread, is not what a single quarterly print costs. (b) The base effects are pure arithmetic over figures NIO itself published on 2025-10-01 (Aug 2025 31,305, Sep 2025 34,749, Q3 2025 87,071); every sell-side model carries the comps, and Benzinga already wired the deceleration narrative on the way to the 52-week low, citing 'recent delivery softness (35,934 units in July versus June's 40,597)' and 'anxiety over China's premium EV pricing landscape ahead of Nio's own second-quarter earnings.' What is genuinely not published is a specific August-2026 estimate -- I searched for a Deutsche Bank August preview and found none. But the hunter's own bottom-up looks wrong-signed: CnEVPost 2026-08-28 puts Onvo L60 at 3,201 units in the first 28 days of August against 4,949 in July, a ~35% fall, and July's ES9 had already slipped to 6,315. 'Flat-to-modestly-up sequentially' is not what that reads; August is more plausibly down from 35,934, which pushes Q3 below the claimed 113-118k. So the direction may hold but the stated magnitude is contested by the same outlet the claim is built on.

findings.finding: NIO's smart-driving chief Ren Shaoqing has founded a separately registered embodied-AI/physical-AI-foundation-model company that has already reached a unicorn-level valuation, and NIO reportedly plans to make a strategic investment in it while Ren stays on as NIO's smart-driving chief. Reported 21 and 24 August 2026, after NIO's last public communication.
findings.adversary_note: The 'no US wire pickup' half of the claim is roughly fair -- I found no Bloomberg/Reuters/Dow Jones item -- but it is not confined to Chinese-language press either. CnEVPost ran it in English twice (2026-08-21 on Ren founding the company, 2026-08-24 on NIO planning to invest and Ren staying on as smart-driving chief), and it was mirrored to moomoo.com, which is a US-facing retail brokerage news feed, plus eletric-vehicles.com, The Electric Viking's stable, digitalphablet and 36kr's English edition. That is exactly the channel a retail-heavy NIO ADS holder reads. What holds the number off 80 is that the item is not connected to this print by anyone. The LatePost report discloses no company name, no investment size and no valuation figure; there is nothing in it that lands in Q2 revenue, Q2 margin or the Q3 guide. It is a governance/key-man and capital-allocation datapoint whose worst realistic expression on 1 September is one analyst question about R&D focus and whether the smart-driving chief's attention is divided -- against a company that just cut 40% of product/software development headcount. The mechanism barely reaches the print, so even a fully unpriced version of it is worth very little on the day.

findings.finding: NIO has now missed its own delivery guidance in consecutive disclosures — June 2026 came in at 40,597 against a 42,900-47,900 guide, and Q2 at 107,658 against 110,000-115,000 — so whatever Q3 unit and revenue range management gives on 1 September starts with an impaired discount factor.
findings.adversary_note: This is the wire copy, and it is also double-counted. The Q2 miss was reported on 1-2 July across CnEVPost, Investing.com, TipRanks, MSN and the Deutsche Bank note syndication; the baseline records a -3.62% move on 2026-07-02, i.e. the price already paid for it. The hunter's own cited source, CnEVPost 2026-08-20, quantifies it to the unit: 'actual deliveries came in 2,342 units (-2.1%) below the low end.' Benzinga's 52-week-low piece names delivery softness and profitability concerns as the reason the stock is where it is. But the more serious problem is that 'consecutive disclosures' is one miss counted twice. NIO never issued a standalone June guide. April was 29,356 and May 37,705, so April+May = 67,061; the Q2 guide of 110,000-115,000 minus 67,061 gives 42,939-47,939 -- which is the claimed '42,900-47,900 June guide' rounded. The June figure and the Q2 figure are the same guidance range measured at two points, and a single 2.1% shortfall cannot be re-served as a pattern of impaired credibility. The claim's premise for a compounding discount factor therefore does not hold, on top of being fully published.

findings.finding: Heidmar's earnings releases are the mechanical trigger for refreshing the resale prospectus covering 11,080,332 shares for B. Riley Principal Capital II: the 424B3 filed 2026-03-24 exists solely to supplement the 20 June 2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' - the same day as the Q4 print. The same pattern holds for 2025-08-12 (two 424B3s the day after the 2025-08-11 print), 2025-09-29 (424B3 and 6-K same day) and 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. That resale registration was re-declared effective 2026-06-10, so 2026-09-01 is the first print under the refreshed shelf, and 11,080,332 shares is 170% of the company's entire non-affiliate share count.
findings.adversary_note: The pattern is real -- I verified 424B3s on 2025-08-12, 2025-09-29, 2025-11-06 and 2026-03-24, and the 2026-03-24 supplement's own text says it supplements the 20-June-2025 prospectus 'with the information contained in our report on Form 6-K, filed with the SEC on March 24, 2026' for 11,080,332 BRPC II shares; the 2025-11-06 supplement says the same for a 6-K filed 2025-11-06, and a POS AM followed the Q1 print by two days. But the fact is published on a retail-facing filing-summary site on each of those days (StockTitan carried '11,080,332 common shares for resale by B. Riley Principal Capital II' on 2026-03-24 and 'registers 11.08M shares; $20M equity facility noted' on 2026-05-29), and the POS AM itself already draws out the dilution-to-float implication verbatim: the shares 'would represent approximately 15.8% of the total number of outstanding Common Shares and approximately 58.6% of the total number of outstanding Common Shares held by non-affiliates.' So the size relative to float is the issuer's own disclosed sentence, not a discovery. More damaging is the flow: the supplements disclose cumulative ELOC usage of 201,682 shares at 2025-09-30 and 215,272 at 2025-12-31 -- about 13,590 shares drawn in all of Q4 2025, 0.02% of shares outstanding per quarter. A prospectus supplement incorporating results is mandatory housekeeping to keep any resale registration usable; it is not a supply event, and management has said it deliberately did not draw at ~$1.27. What survives is narrow but genuine: nobody has published that the earnings 6-K is the mechanical trigger, and nobody has connected the refreshed-effective shelf to the fact that spot at $1.38 now clears the CEO's own stated reservation price. That inference is unpublished and reaches tomorrow.

findings.finding: The two-analyst FY2026 revenue forecast of $74.29m implies roughly $18.6m per quarter for Q2-Q4 against Q1 2026 actual of $18.4m - i.e. essentially flat, and below Q4 2025's $25.1m - while the spot rates that drive both of Heidmar's revenue lines rose 47-82% sequentially in Q2 (Frontline realised VLCC $103,500 to $152,700/day, Suezmax $72,400 to $111,500/day, LR2/Aframax $50,700 to $92,400/day, Q1 to Q2 2026), and the five vessels added in March/April 2026 contribute a full quarter for the first time. Heidmar's Q1 revenue was $5.68m trade revenues plus $12.67m voyage and time charter revenues from eight vessels employed on short-term spot/TC voyages versus one a year earlier; the Q2 2025 comparative is $9.6m total revenue and $0.5m adjusted net income.
findings.adversary_note: The rate data is not merely public, it is the single most-covered story in shipping this quarter. Frontline printed a record Q2 on 2026-08-28 with VLCC TCE of $152,700/day, Lloyd's List called the 2026 tanker boom the second-best in history on the same week, Teekay reported near-record midsize rates, and the trade press has noted this is the fourth consecutive quarter of six-figure VLCC earnings -- so the sequential step-up is an increment inside a boom already running four quarters, not a regime change. Heidmar's own leverage to it is also pre-narrated: the CEO told Capital Link on 2026-02-19 the company is 'a proxy for the tanker market' with earnings responding directly to freight through management fees and revenue-sharing, and quoted VLCCs at ~$120,000/day. The sell-side has already revised up -- Maxim's Tate Sullivan raised FY2026 and FY2027 revenue and EBITDA after the Q1 print and lifted the target to $2.25, 63% above spot. Most decisively, the tape: HMR went $1.11 on 2026-08-03 to $1.45 on 2026-08-20 and $1.38 on 08-31, and that window is exactly the tanker peer reporting season. The +24.33% 20-day run-up is the read-through being paid for. The genuinely obscure part is only the arithmetic -- that a two-analyst FY2026 revenue print of $74.29m backs into ~$18.6m quarters -- and I could not locate that number published anywhere, but a two-analyst consensus on a foreign-private-issuer de-SPAC is not the price-setting benchmark: Q1 missed the revenue 'consensus' by 32% and the stock has since risen roughly 25% off the low. Note also that most of the sequential revenue swing sits in the $12.67m voyage-and-time-charter line, which is gross freight on chartered-in tonnage with hire cost against it, so a large revenue beat does not translate proportionally to net income.

findings.finding: Heidmar's fee-earning commercially managed fleet was effectively flat through Q2 2026: the 2025 Form 20-F filed 2026-04-30 states 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar', while the 2026-07-07 release states the company manages 'around 50 vessels under commercial management and 16 vessels under technical management' - and that is after an acquisition (Q-Shipping B.V., effective 2026-07-01) that the company itself says added nine vessels to the managed fleet. Heidmar has issued no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19, the longest such gap since the de-SPAC, against five additions announced for Q1.
findings.adversary_note: I think this one is largely a category error rather than a discovery. Q-Shipping B.V. is a ship-management and crewing business and the nine vessels it brought are 'a mix of bulk carriers, general cargo vessels, and chemical/product tankers' -- those belong in TECHNICAL management, not the commercial pool count the 20-F's '49 vessels' refers to. The published series bears that out: Capital Link 2026-02-19 quotes 'about 40 tankers under commercial management and 10 under technical management'; the 2026-07-07 release says 'around 50 under commercial management and 16 under technical management.' Technical went 10 to 16 across the period that contains the acquisition. Total managed therefore went from 49-50 to ~66, an increase of roughly a third, not 'effectively flat.' Second, the 49-versus-50 gap the claim leans on is rounding inside a single document: the same 20-F fleet table (5 VLCC, 9 Suezmax, 4 LR2, 2 LR1, 11 MR, 7 Aframax, 3 small, 1 PSV, 5 bulkers, 3 broker) is described by screeners as '50 vessels as of April 30, 2026.' Third, the claim's own supporting assertion -- 'no fleet-addition press release since 2026-05-19' -- is contradicted by the 2026-07-07 release it cites in the same sentence. Fourth, sizing: pool and management fees are a minority of an $18.4m quarter, and a plus-or-minus-four swing in commercial vessel count is a rounding error against a 47-82% sequential rate move. What is unpriced is only the negative inference itself, which nobody has drawn -- because it is probably not true.

findings.finding: Heidmar has had no Chief Financial Officer since 31 May 2026 - Niki Fotiou ceased in the role and CEO Pankaj Khanna took over 'the finance function' pending a search - and no successor has been announced as of 2026-08-31, three months later. Q2 2026 is therefore the first quarter this company has closed, audited-reviewed and reported without a CFO. Separately, Heidmar has furnished no Form 6-K since 2026-05-28 despite three subsequent material announcements (CFO departure, Nasdaq compliance regained, Q-Shipping acquisition).
findings.adversary_note: The departure is wire copy, not a discovery. GlobeNewswire on 2026-06-01, then Investing.com, TradeWinds ('Heidmar hunts new finance chief as Niki Fotiou leaves after three years'), StockTitan, TipRanks/theFly, GuruFocus, Manila Times and Yahoo all carried it inside 24 hours, including the detail that Khanna would oversee the finance function pending a search. That no successor has been named is verifiable by anyone in ten seconds from the empty news record -- Heidmar has issued exactly four press releases between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-31 -- so 'Q2 is the first quarter closed without a CFO' is an inference that requires no work and confers no informational edge. The 'no 6-K since 2026-05-28' half I confirmed on EDGAR, but it does not support the reading placed on it: a foreign private issuer is not required to furnish a 6-K for every press release, and all three subsequent items were press-released and wire-covered, so nothing was withheld from the market. What is left is a genuine but small residual -- elevated risk of a delayed or thin release, or a weaker MD&A, on a print where the date has already been company-confirmed for 2026-09-01 pre-open.

findings.finding: Only 6,498,572 of Heidmar's 58,991,997 outstanding shares are held by non-affiliates - an 11.0% float worth about $9.0m at spot - against 20-day average volume of 50,189 shares and short interest of just 127,609 shares. The prospectus states verbatim: 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company.'
findings.adversary_note: The premise is refuted. The claim rests on 'every screener reports the 59m count' as float; both of the most-used free screeners report the small float, and report it smaller than the prospectus does. stockanalysis.com shows shares outstanding 58.99m, float 6.07m, insider ownership 89.71%, institutions 0.40%; finviz shows Shs Outstand 58.99M, Shs Float 5.53M, Insider Own 90.62%. So a ~10% float is on the free web, not buried in a POS AM. The prospectus quote itself is accurate -- I read p12151143_pos-am.htm and it says verbatim 'As of May 20, 2026, we had 58,991,997 Common Shares outstanding, of which 6,498,572 shares were held by non-affiliates of our company' -- but the number it produces is larger than what the screeners already publish, so the finding, if acted on, corrects the price in the wrong direction. Separately, this is a width fact and not a directional one, and the width is already in the baseline: 71.9% annualised realised vol on 50,189 shares a day and a 5.13% median print reaction are exactly what a 5-6m share float on an $83m de-SPAC produces. Finally the brief's short-interest figure of 127,609 shares is not confirmed by either screener (53,874 and ~50,000).

findings.finding: Three Heidmar directors filed Form 144s to sell 244,862 shares between 2026-06-11 and 2026-07-06 - Andreas Konialidis 113,287 shares ($165,400), Vasileios Loutradis 126,575 shares ($138,699) and Andre Lockhorst 5,000 shares ($5,950) - equal to about 3.8% of the entire non-affiliate float and roughly five sessions of average volume. Both larger sellers were disposing of 104,954-share awards dated 2026-04-01, i.e. registering to sell within ten weeks of the grant. As a foreign private issuer there is no Form 4 to confirm execution.
findings.adversary_note: The documents check out -- I read two of the three primary_doc.xml files directly (Loutradis 126,575 shares, $138,699, broker Piraeus Securities S.A., sale date 2026-06-26, of which 104,954 were an employee stock award dated 2026-04-01; Lockhorst 5,000 shares, $5,950, sale date 2026-07-08, board compensation acquired 2025-07-18) -- but the finding fails on both publication and timing. All three 144s are indexed with headlines on StockTitan on their filing dates (06/11 'Affiliate files sale notice for HMR common stock', 06/26 'Piraeus Securities lists proposed Common Stock sales for HMR', 07/06), which is where retail sees insider filings on a name this size. And the mechanism does not reach tomorrow: the stated sale dates were in June and July, the Rule 144 windows from those filings are expired or nearly so, and whatever selling occurred passed through the tape during a period in which the stock rose from $1.11 to $1.38. This is supply behind us, not overhang into the print. Sizing kills the rest: 244,862 shares is 0.41% of shares outstanding and about $338k at $1.38 -- real against a 5-6m float, trivial against an $83m cap. Two smaller points: the 3.8% figure uses the 6,498,572 denominator that h1#4 supplies, and both screeners put the float below that, so the true percentage is nearer 4.4%; and Loutradis received employee stock awards, so describing all three sellers as 'directors' is loose.

findings.finding: Half of Heidmar's fee base sits with one related party that has just been separately capitalised: the 20-F states the Capital vessels are 25 of 49 managed vessels and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', and Capital Tankers Corp. listed on Euronext Growth Oslo on 2026-03-17 after raising about USD 500m, with a fleet of 30 super-eco crude tankers of which 21 are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028 plus options on 13 more.
findings.adversary_note: Every component is published, and the most important one was pre-announced by management. The concentration is the 20-F's own related-party disclosure -- 'The Capital vessels compose 25 of the 49 vessels currently managed by Heidmar' and 'accounted for 37% of our total revenues from the Pools during the year ended December 31, 2025', with Capital owned by the father of the indirect owner of Maistros Shipinvest, a Heidmar major shareholder -- filed 2026-04-30 and summarised by StockTitan the same week. The Capital Tankers listing was not obscure: Euronext's own press release called the NOK 4.8bn / ~USD 500m placement 'the largest western shipping listing in the last two decades' on 2026-03-17, and it was covered by MarketScreener, elnavi and the shipping trades. Crucially, the CEO had already told investors on 2026-02-19 to expect 'roughly 30 newbuilding vessels to enter its platform over the next two years' -- that is the Capital Tankers pipeline, disclosed a month before the listing. And the direction is ambiguous: the same fact is a customer-concentration risk and a funded newbuild pipeline flowing into Heidmar's pools. Nothing here lands inside a Q2 print: 21 of the 30 vessels are newbuildings delivering 2026-2028, so the fee impact is quarters and years out, not tomorrow morning.

findings.finding: The syndicated Q1 FY27 consensus revenue of $9.47bn (+10.4% on the $8,578m year-ago base) sits roughly a point below what Medtronic's own 3 June quarterly guidance implies — 11.5% to 12.0% organic growth plus a 'neutral to $50 million' FX tailwind plus acquired revenue from CathWorks/Scientia/SPR, i.e. about $9.55-9.65bn — while consensus EPS of $1.39 is exactly the midpoint of the guided $1.38-$1.40; the same one-point gap exists at the full-year level ($38.85bn consensus vs 6.75-7.25% organic on $36,364m plus 0-1% FX plus M&A). The likeliest cause is incomplete modelling of the 53rd selling week, which management sized at 500-600bps of Q1 revenue but 600-700bps of Q1 EPS, so the EPS line was captured and part of the revenue line was not. Mechanically this makes a print that merely lands on guidance read in the wire copy as a $100-180m top-line beat.
findings.adversary_note: I did the arithmetic and the claim is directionally right but materially over-sized, and its conclusion is already published sell-side copy. Guidance-implied: 8,578 x 1.115 = 9,564 and x 1.12 = 9,607, plus 0-50 FX gives 9,564-9,657, plus small CathWorks/Scientia/SPR revenue (Medtronic's stated organic definition does exclude 'significant acquisitions') gives roughly 9.58-9.71bn. The problem is the other side of the subtraction: $9.47bn is the Zacks panel only. The consensus quoted in today's Investing.com preview (2026-08-31) and in the optionstradingreport piece (2026-08-29) is $9.55bn, +11.3%, which sits INSIDE the hunter's own guidance-implied range and only ~0.9% below its midpoint, not 'a point below' the whole range. The 500-600bps extra-selling-week revenue tailwind is quantified verbatim in that same 2026-08-31 preview, so the 53rd week is in the wire copy, not missed. And the inference -- that a print merely on guidance reads as a beat-and-raise -- is exactly Needham's published note of 2026-08-27 (PT $101 to $114, Buy, 'expects Medtronic to beat consensus revenue and EPS' and 'to raise its full-year FY2027 revenue and earnings guidance', citing 'management's conservative guidance'). The 'EPS captured, revenue not' diagnosis is also a non-sequitur: analysts anchor EPS to guided midpoints as routine practice and build revenue bottom-up conservatively; that pattern is present in almost every MDT quarter and does not evidence a modelling error. Finally, the option chain has already taken the bullish side of this: ~10 calls per put on volume and 18,801 Sep $100 calls traded against 1,704 OI, publicly reported since 2026-08-11. Residual value is the small headline delta against the lagging Zacks aggregate.

findings.finding: As of 2026-08-31 no registration statement or tender-offer document for the MiniMed split-off exists on EDGAR: Medtronic (CIK 1613103) has filed no 8-K since 2026-06-03 and no S-4/Schedule TO, and MiniMed Group (CIK 2062583) shows no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO on or after 2026-06-01. On 3 June management said separation was expected 'prior to year-end' and explicitly framed early separation as potential upside to FY27 guidance, which assumes twelve months of Diabetes consolidation. An exchange offer needs a registered offer document and a ~20-business-day offer period, so with nothing on file at end-August the 'upside from early separation' has not begun to be executed. Compounding it, MMED traded at $18.92 on 2026-08-26, below its $20.00 March IPO price, which weakens the discount economics of a split-off and raises the odds of a plain pro-rata spin-off that would retire none of Medtronic's ~1.28bn shares.
findings.adversary_note: The docket facts check out -- MDT's last 8-K is 2026-06-03 with no S-4/SC TO, and MiniMed's filing history since 2026-06-01 is 8-K (06-29, 08-05), 10-K (06-29), DEF 14A/DEFA14A/ARS (08-21) and Forms 3/4, with no S-4, S-1, 425 or SC TO. But the market-relevant fact is not the docket, it is 'no separation transaction has been launched', and that is trivially known to every holder because a launch is a press-released, 8-K'd event. More damaging, the published expectation is a split-off around six months after the 2026-03-09 IPO close -- i.e. around 2026-09-09 -- so an empty docket on 2026-08-31 is ON schedule, not late, and the inference that 'early separation upside has not begun to be executed' does not follow: FY27 runs to late April 2027, leaving roughly eight months, and an S-1/S-4 plus a 20-business-day offer easily fits. There is also a real chance the next step is announced on this very call, which would invert the finding's sign. The MMED-below-$20 half is analytically wrong: split-off exchange-offer economics turn on the discount to MMED's prevailing market price and on MDT's own valuation, not on the March IPO price, which is a sunk reference with no role in the exchange ratio. And MMED at $18.92 sits against a 52-week high of $20.88 set 2026-08-13 and a BofA target raised to $24 on 2026-08-10 -- hardly a broken deal. The only genuinely unpriced residual is a mild disappointment if management gives no separation update tomorrow, and that is worth almost nothing against a 4.57% implied move.

findings.finding: The Investor Day Medtronic committed to on 2025-08-19, when it added two Elliott-adjacent directors and formed the Growth and Operating Committees, was promised for 'mid-calendar year 2026' and was to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the committees' margin and efficiency targets. Mid-2026 has passed and, as of 2026-08-31, no date has been announced: the June Q4 call did not mention it and the Medtronic newsroom shows only three releases since (21 July Touch Surgery Aide, 6 August Affera CE Mark, 20 August dividend).
findings.adversary_note: I concede the facts. The 2025-08-19 release does promise an Investor Day in 'mid-calendar year 2026' to lay out the go-forward financial algorithm and the Growth/Operating Committee work; I searched the 2026-06-03 Q4 transcript and found no mention of 'investor day', 'Growth Committee' or 'Operating Committee' at all; the 2026-03-03 CFO-conference release lists only Barclays and Leerink fireside chats; and I found no article anywhere noting the slip. So the observation is genuinely unpublished. What sinks it is the other three tests. The underlying promise is not obscure -- it is in a Medtronic press release and in every Elliott-stake story from Fierce, MDDI, Star Tribune and Hedgeweek -- and its non-occurrence is checkable on a public IR calendar in ten seconds, which is not the profile of information the marginal holder is unaware of. The mechanism also does not reach this print: an investor-day date is not a Q1 line item, nothing about it resolves in the 2026-09-01 release, and the sign is ambiguous in a way the finding does not acknowledge -- the single most likely place a date gets announced is tomorrow's call, in which case the absence today is a setup for a positive, not a negative. Against a $117bn cap with 29 analysts and a 4.57% implied move, a soft governance-timing slip that no one has written about is worth roughly a tenth of a percent.

findings.finding: Boston Scientific reported on 2026-07-29 that its electrophysiology business grew only 3% in the US in calendar Q2 2026 (versus 23% internationally), citing competitive pressure and noting that US PFA is now roughly 80% of the AFib market. Calendar Q2 covers about two-thirds of Medtronic's fiscal Q1 (25 April to 31 July), and Cardiac Ablation Solutions — up 78% globally and 124% in the US in Medtronic's Q4 FY26 — is the single largest contributor to the 6.75-7.25% FY27 organic guide. The datapoint reads as continued Affera/Sphere-9 share gain in the quarter Medtronic is about to report, but the same disclosure caps how much market growth is left.
findings.adversary_note: This is a wire event, not a discovery. Boston Scientific's 2026-07-29 release and call are the source, the numbers are as stated (EP +9% organic, +3% US, +23% ex-US; US PFA ~80% of the AFib market; H2 global EP growth guided flat), and the second guidance cut of the year was covered the same day by MedTech Dive, MassDevice and MDDI with the read-across spelled out explicitly -- 'heavier competition in electrophysiology... including pressure from Medtronic' and management conceding it 'undercalled how much rivals would take'. There is no interpretive step left for a hunter to add. It also shows in the tape: MDT closed $84.22 on 2026-07-27 and traded $90-94 through August, and the Zacks preview already names Cardiac Ablation Solutions as 'the key growth driver' with PFA up 145% last quarter, while Needham's 2026-08-27 upgrade cites Affera momentum by name. The penetration-ceiling half is marginally less connected to this specific print -- a saturation argument bites on FY28 durability rather than on a fiscal Q1 that ended 2026-07-31 -- but it too is in the published BSX disclosure and is a standard bear point in MDT coverage. Note also the two halves partially offset each other in sign, which caps whatever residual exists.

findings.finding: MMED's short interest is 5,896,696 shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a public float of 27.96m shares (Medtronic holds ~90% of 280.84m shares outstanding) - i.e. ~21% of float with 5.1-5.7 days to cover - yet the most widely syndicated short-interest pages display it as '2.1% of float' because they divide by shares outstanding rather than float; the position was built from 1,341,393 shares at the 2026-03-13 settlement to a 6,570,728 peak on 2026-06-30 and has been reduced only ~10% since, while the stock has roughly doubled off its 2026-05-15 low of $10.65.
findings.adversary_note: The load-bearing part of this claim -- that the correct denominator is hidden -- is false. StockAnalysis.com displays 'Short % of Float: 21.09%' explicitly alongside 'Short % of Shares Out 2.10%', and Finviz displays 'Short Float 22.59%' on float of 26.10m; those are two of the most-used free screens in existence. MarketBeat (the hunter's own source) is the outlier that divides by outstanding. The underlying data is FINRA bi-weekly public data, and the borrow desk prices utilisation regardless of any web rendering. Separately, the interpretation is likely wrong: in a pending parent/sub split-off the standard arb is long parent / short sub to capture the exchange-offer discount, so a large slice of 5.9m shares short in a 28m float is structural stub arb, not directional bears, and does not behave like squeeze fuel into an EPS print. The one genuinely useful residual is mechanical: 21% of float short in a 28m float amplifies whatever the print does, and that is consistent with the single observed reaction of +15.93% on 2026-06-03 -- i.e. already demonstrated once, in the tape.

findings.finding: The IPO lock-up lapses on the morning of the print: the 424B4 is dated 2026-03-05 and EDGAR full-text search confirms it contains the phrase '180 days after the date of this prospectus' (180 days from 2026-03-05 is 2026-09-01), and that lock-up binds Medtronic's ~252.9m shares as well as every officer and director; as of 2026-08-31 Medtronic's EDGAR submissions show no S-4, no Schedule TO and no 425 has ever been filed, so the split-off exchange offer is not launched and becomes launchable from this print forward against a stated intent to finish the separation in calendar 2026.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves of the fact are verified and both are already published or trivially derivable. MarketBeat's syndicated IPO lock-up expiration calendar carries MMED with an expiry of 9/2/2026 -- one day off the hunter's date, on a page that exists precisely so retail can see this. And 180 days from a prospectus dated 2026-03-05 is arithmetic anybody can do from a document that has been on EDGAR for six months. The mechanism is the weaker part. Medtronic has stated since 2025 that it intends a 'generally tax-free' distribution structured as spin-off, split-off or combination; a cash sale of the retained stake would be taxable and would jeopardise 355 treatment, so a lock-up lapse is not a supply event for this holder. Carve-out lock-ups also routinely except transfers made in connection with the separation, meaning the lock-up was never the binding constraint on the split-off. And Medtronic's own FY26 Q4 release guides FY27 EPS on an assumption of 'consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27' -- which is the opposite of an offer that becomes live the morning of this print. The residual novelty is only the date coincidence with the print, which is real but nearly worthless.

findings.finding: MiniMed's Senior VP, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Courtney Nelson Wills, notified the company on 2026-07-30 that she is resigning effective 2026-09-25 after an eight-week transition - disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-08-05, i.e. she departs inside the exact window in which a tax-free split-off exchange offer, an S-4 and ~160 Medtronic transition-services agreements have to be executed.
findings.adversary_note: This is a filed 8-K from 2026-08-05 that was picked up and headlined by StockTitan ('MiniMed General Counsel Courtney Nelson Wills to resign'), so it is published, not obscure. The 8-K itself pre-empts the hunter's framing: it states she is leaving for personal reasons having accepted a role outside the medical device industry, that the departure is not due to any disagreement with the company, and that a successor search is underway. A general counsel departure with an eight-week transition is not a material driver of a revenue-and-EPS print, and the connection drawn to the split-off execution window is inference layered on a routine disclosure rather than a new fact. Twenty-six days have passed since filing with no visible reaction in a stock whose 20-day run-up is +4.55%.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 is a 14-week quarter and the two halves of the arithmetic sit in two different companies' disclosures: MiniMed's CFO said on 2026-06-03 that 'excluding the extra week, we expect Q1 growth to be roughly similar to Q4' (Q4 FY26 organic was 8.7%), while Medtronic's CFO quantified the extra selling week as '500 to 600 basis points to first-quarter growth' - stacking them implies MMED prints roughly 14% organic growth, versus the '~10% organic FY27 outlook' that quote pages and screens carry as the company's guidance.
findings.adversary_note: This is arithmetically neutralised by the published consensus. The prior-year comparable quarter (Medtronic Diabetes, quarter ended 2025-07-25) was $721m, reported 2025-08-19. The consensus in the pre-print wire is $828.43m. That is +14.9% reported, and with EURUSD y/y essentially flat (+0.3% on the hunter's own, verified, monthly averages) reported and organic converge -- so the sell-side is already modelling roughly 14-15% organic, which is precisely what the hunter's 'stacking' produces. The premise that the market is anchored to '~10% organic' for this quarter also fails at source: MiniMed's own 2026-06-03 release states FY27 organic growth of approximately 10% 'which includes a 1.0 to 1.5% expected benefit from the extra week in FY27' -- the extra week is inside the guidance sentence, not hidden behind it, and pushing a 1.0-1.5% full-year benefit into the one quarter that contains the whole 53rd week gives ~5-6%, which is exactly the Medtronic CFO's 500-600bps. Nothing here is a surprise to anyone who read the guidance line. The only residual is the small chance the buy-side has not done the Q1 concentration, which the $828m print-level consensus argues against.

findings.finding: MiniMed's fiscal Q1 FY27 is a 98-day (14-week) quarter — 2026-04-25 through 2026-07-31 — against a 91-day (13-week) prior-year quarter (2025-04-26 through 2025-07-25); the entire 53rd week of FY27 falls in this single quarter, and MiniMed's own definition of 'Organic Revenue Growth' adjusts only for FX and Italian payback accruals, NOT for extra weeks, so the organic-growth headline will print roughly double the 8.7% it printed for Q4 FY26 on calendar alone. The dates are established by the company's own filings: FY26 ended 2026-04-24 (Q4 exhibit 99.1), the year-ago quarter ended 2025-07-25 (Medtronic 10-Q mdt-20250725), and this quarter ends 2026-07-31 (the 2026-07-20 announcement).
findings.adversary_note: The fiscal arithmetic checks out -- 2026-04-25 to 2026-07-31 is 98 days (6+31+30+31) against 2025-04-26 to 2025-07-25 at 91 days (5+31+30+25), and the 53rd week does land entirely in this quarter -- but the company pre-disclosed it in the same press release the hunter cites as its source. Exhibit 99.1 of 2026-06-03 says FY27 organic growth of approximately 10% 'includes a 1.0 to 1.5% expected benefit from the extra week in FY27', and Medtronic's parallel release says FY27 guidance 'incorporates the 53rd week impact'. Sell-side consensus of $828.43m against a $721m comp is +14.9%, which cannot be reached without the extra week, so the inflation is in the number the print will be judged against. The magnitude claim also overshoots: 8.7% plus ~5.5% is ~14%, which is 1.6x the 8.7%, not 'roughly double'. What remains is a presentational caution about a headline that the analysts already discount, not a fact the marginal holder lacks.

findings.finding: The euro tailwind that supplied roughly half of Q4 FY26's reported-vs-organic gap (15.6% reported vs 8.7% organic) is gone in this quarter: EURUSD monthly averages for May/Jun/Jul 2026 were 1.1681/1.1510/1.1419 (avg 1.1536) versus 1.1276/1.1518/1.1698 a year earlier (avg 1.1497) — +0.34% y/y, against +8.2% y/y for the Feb-Apr window that Q4 FY26 covered. MiniMed's 10-K puts OUS revenue at ~70% of FY26 total (Q4 FY26: international $599m of $837m, US only $238m), making it one of the most FX-levered US-listed medtechs.
findings.adversary_note: The FX data is correct -- I verified the 2026 monthly EURUSD averages on x-rates (May 1.1681, Jun 1.1510, Jul 1.1419) -- but currency is the single most explicitly modelled line item on any sell-side medtech model, and MiniMed's own disclosures make its FX leverage impossible to miss: FY26 reported +14.2% against organic +8.0% is 620bps of published FX, and Q4's $599m international against $238m US is in the earnings release. Medtronic guides currency explicitly ('neutral to 1% accretive' for FY27, 2026-06-03). Most decisively, the consensus revenue of $828.43m against a $721m comp implies +14.9% reported, which is only consistent with FX at roughly flat -- so the collapse of the reported-vs-organic gap is already inside the number the print will be measured against. The claim is a correct observation about a variable the street updates weekly.

findings.finding: About $20m of Q4 FY26's $837m reported revenue was not product demand: the 'Other' line jumped to $22m from $2m a year earlier and the footnote defines it as 'net sales generated from the sales of smart insulin pens and services. Amounts in this line also reflect adjustments to the Company's Italian payback accruals' — a legal-accrual release that is expressly excluded from the organic growth definition. Anyone extrapolating the $837m base into Q1 has carried a one-off forward, and the underlying Italian exposure is live rather than settled: the Council of State (Ordinance No. 1589/2026) suspended industry appeals against the Ministry of Health decree of 29 December 2023 and referred the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Italian Constitutional Court.
findings.adversary_note: The $22m-vs-$2m 'Other' line and its footnote are in the 2026-06-03 earnings release, filed with the SEC and reproduced by the wires, and the company's own organic definition tells you plainly that the Italian payback adjustment is excluded -- so the accounting fact is published and self-flagged. The mechanism to this print is where it breaks down: consensus is built year-over-year off a $721m comparable, not sequentially off $837m, so 'anyone extrapolating $837m into Q1' describes a modelling error the sell-side has not made, and the accrual release sits in the base quarter rather than in the quarter being reported. The Council of State Ordinance No. 1589/2026 and the Constitutional Court referral are genuinely obscure -- confirmed only in Italian law-firm commentary, not in any equity research or wire copy I can find -- which is the one part of this that earns credit; but the Constitutional Court has already upheld the payback mechanism twice (rulings 139/2024 and 140/2024), the exposure is disclosed, and the timing of an Italian constitutional referral does not land inside a September 1 print. Roughly 2.4% of one quarter's revenue in a base period is not a share-price event.

findings.finding: The US business — the whole basis of the Flex equity story — grew 1.5% in Q4 FY26 ($238m of $837m) versus +12.2% organic internationally, and the reporting quarter cannot show the Flex inflection because Flex's actual differentiator arrived after quarter end: MiniMed's 2026-08-17 release says Flex 'now shipping' with Abbott's 15-day Instinct sensor, 17 days after the 2026-07-31 close, while the 2026-06-17 US launch release told customers the Instinct pairing was investigational and 'expected later in summer 2026'. The company therefore told prospective US pump buyers, inside the quarter, that a materially better bundle was weeks away.
findings.adversary_note: Every factual component is a press release with trade-press pickup. The 2026-06-17 US Flex launch release stated the Instinct pairing was investigational and would follow 'later this summer'; the 2026-08-17 release announced Flex now shipping with Instinct, covered by MedTech Dive, MassDevice, DrugDeliveryBusiness, PR Newswire, Nasdaq and StockTitan; and the US/international split (US $238m, +1.5%, versus +12.2% organic international) is in the Q4 release, with the 10-K stating US +2% versus international +21% for the full year. So the weak-US, strong-international shape is known to the point of being the consensus criticism of the name -- and the market saw it in the Q4 release and still marked the stock +15.93%. The genuinely unpublished part is the inference that US pump buyers deferred inside the quarter because they had been told a better bundle was weeks away; that is a real, unmodelled second-order effect on one revenue line, but it is an inference, it is small, and it points the same direction as a US line the street already writes down. Note the 8/17 shipping announcement -- the offsetting forward positive -- produced no visible move in a tape that is +4.55% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Medtronic's April 2026 intrusion (ShinyHunters, unauthorised access 13-19 April 2026) resulted in notification of 3,834,294 individuals, with letters going out from late June into July 2026 — squarely inside MiniMed's fiscal Q1 — and several class actions already filed; exposed fields include Social Security numbers and health information. MiniMed filed its own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident on 2026-04-27 saying it was 'not aware of any compromises to the IT systems used by its business', but it has never quantified exposure, and the Q1 10-Q is the first periodic filing that must address it while MiniMed still runs on Medtronic IT under the separation arrangements.
findings.adversary_note: This was a wire story across the security and healthcare press in late June and early July 2026 -- SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer, HIPAA Journal, SecurityAffairs, Rescana -- with the 3,834,294 figure, the 13-19 April access window, the SSN/health-data fields and the class actions all reported. It is also Medtronic's incident, not MiniMed's, and MiniMed's own 2026-04-27 Reg-FD 8-K said it was not aware of compromises to its business systems. The claim's distinguishing hook is factually shaky: MiniMed filed its FY26 10-K on 2026-06-29, two months after the intrusion, so the Q1 10-Q is not the first periodic filing that must address it. No dollar exposure has been quantified by anyone, remediation costs of this kind land at the parent, and a breach disclosure in a 10-Q filed alongside a beat-or-miss revenue print is not what moves a 28m-float stock.

findings.finding: Informative absence on the largest feared mechanical event: as of 2026-08-31 neither Medtronic (CIK 0001613103) nor MiniMed (CIK 0002062583) has filed a Form S-4, Schedule TO or Form 425 for the split-off exchange offer, so an exchange offer cannot legally launch in the days around this print, and Medtronic's FY27 EPS guidance still 'assumes consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27'. Separation groundwork is visibly proceeding but at governance pace, not offer pace — the board went from 9 to 11 on 2026-06-29 adding Alcon CEO David Endicott as an independent director, and the first annual meeting is set for 2026-10-09.
findings.adversary_note: I verified the docket absence independently and the hunter is right on the facts -- no S-4, Schedule TO, TO-C, TO-I, 425 or SC 14D9 for either CIK -- but the reassuring inference is drawn straight from the most-read Medtronic document of the year. Medtronic's own FY26 Q4 press release of 2026-06-03 states its FY27 EPS guidance assumes 'consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27' and that 'while an offering and split-off is the company's current preferred separation structure, a final decision has not been reached at this time'. Any MDT-covering analyst read that sentence in June. The corroborating governance items are likewise public and syndicated: the board expansion 8-K of 2026-06-29 and the DEF 14A of 2026-08-21 setting the first annual meeting for 2026-10-09. So the 'informative absence' is an absence anyone can see in a free EDGAR query, over-determined by a guidance sentence in a widely-read release. Where it retains a little value is as the correct resolution of the lock-up question that its counterpart finding gets wrong -- which makes it more useful as a corrective than as new information.

findings.finding: Zepp set its H2 2026 margin expectations on 8 June 2026 with CFO Leon Deng naming memory as the specific gross-margin risk ("we expect higher memory costs to create near-term pressure on gross margins, driven by the industry-wide transition from DDR4 to DDR5 and high-bandwidth memory") and naming ASP increases plus a possible tariff refund as the offsets; since that date the consumer DRAM squeeze has escalated sharply — TrendForce on 22 June 2026 said consumer DRAM shortages had cascaded all the way down to DDR2 (contract prices +35-40% QoQ in 3Q26) and that OEMs/ODMs were substituting DDR4 designs with DDR3 and DDR3 with DDR2 to hold system cost. Zepp's gross margin had already fallen from a company-record 40.4% in Q4 2025 to 37.7% in Q1 2026, so the 1 September margin print and the H2 margin commentary are being made into a materially worse cost environment than the one management described in June.
findings.adversary_note: Both halves are published, and the more important half was published BY MANAGEMENT into a 28.6% down day. Deng's exact memory-cost warning is in the Q1 transcript (fool.com, 2026-06-10) and in the Q1 press release ('elevated memory component costs... DDR4 to DDR5'), and ZEPP fell 28.64% on the 2026-06-09 print -- the margin-under-memory-pressure narrative is the single most recently repriced fact on this name. The escalation half is not obscure either: the 2025-26 memory squeeze has its own Wikipedia article, CNBC (2026-01-10), The Register (2026-02-02) and Tom's Hardware coverage of Q3 2026 pricing, plus Apple raising hardware prices on 2026-06-25 and Cisco flagging ~200bps of margin erosion. The specific TrendForce DDR2 datapoint was syndicated to EE Times Asia, TechPowerUp and VideoCardz on/after 2026-06-22, i.e. eight days before the quarter being reported even closed. Two further deductions: the +35-40% figure is a 3Q26 contract price and therefore cannot sit in an Apr-Jun cost of goods sold at all (the Q2-relevant number is the +55-60% already in the same TrendForce release), and TrendForce's own follow-up (2026-07-03) says 3Q26 gains moderate as consumer demand weakens. What is left unpriced is narrow: that legacy-node substitution (DDR4->DDR3->DDR2) is precisely the memory tier a wearable uses, so Zepp's exposure is worse than the generic 'DDR5 transition' framing management gave. That residual is real but small against a memory BOM of a few hundred megabytes per watch.

findings.finding: The Balance 3 / Balance Ultra family, announced 2 June 2026 and presented as 'launched' in the Q1 release six days later, did not actually go on sale until the turn of June and July 2026 (Balance Ultra and Balance 3 Stainless Steel at the turn of the month, Balance 3 Titanium 'a few weeks later'). So the quarter being reported on 1 September carries essentially none of the new flagship line, while Q3 is the first quarter to carry both $599.99 SKUs (Balance Ultra and Cheetah 2 Ultra) — against a backdrop where portfolio ASPs rose more than 20% YoY in Q1 2026 and all seven 2026 launches were holding at MSRP with no discounting.
findings.adversary_note: The factual premise is contested by the company's own primary document. Zepp's Business Wire release of 2026-06-02 states Balance Ultra and Balance 3 Stainless Steel are 'available starting June 2, 2026' at $599.99/$369.99 with Balance 3 Titanium 'coming soon' at $449.99, and secondary coverage records pre-orders from June 2 with shipping mid-June. The5krunner's 'turn of June and July' is one niche blog's reading, explicitly caveated for European variation, and it is the only support the claim has. Even taking the blog at face value, the conclusion is structural rather than discovered: a flagship announced 2026-06-02 into a quarter closing 2026-06-30 obviously contributes little, and management set the $63-68m Q2 revenue guide on 2026-06-08 with full knowledge of the actual ship dates -- so any Q2 shortfall from launch timing is inside the guide, not outside it. The forward half (Q3 first quarter with two $599.99 SKUs, ASPs +20% YoY, no discounting) is the bull case management itself made on the June call and the5krunner already published on 2026-06-09; what it lacks is not publication but conviction, which is exactly why the stock is 91.8% off its high. The only genuinely unpriced element is whether the 1 September Q3 revenue guide comes in above the mechanical seasonal step-up, and that is an outcome, not a finding.

findings.finding: Zepp quietly exited Oura's ITC Section 337 case: Oura and Zepp jointly asked the ITC to terminate Zepp from Investigation No. 337-TA-1468 on 9 July 2026 and the administrative law judge granted it on 10 July 2026, removing the risk of a US limited exclusion order against the Amazfit Helio Ring ahead of the Helio Ring 2 and Helio Strap 2 launches confirmed for H2 2026. Terms were not disclosed, so a settlement or royalty charge could surface in the Q3 numbers rather than Q2.
findings.adversary_note: The event is real and I verified it, but it has been reported at three levels of visibility across seven weeks, the top one being Bloomberg Law. Bloomberg Law carried 'Zepp Drops Patent Suit Against Oura Over Fitness Tracking Tech' off the 2026-07-10 dismissal notice; the ITC issued its determination not to review on 2026-08-11 and published the notice 2026-08-12, which is a public docket entry; and gadgetsandwearables laid the whole thing out including the joint 2026-07-09 motion and the settlement basis on 2026-08-21, ten days before the print. The hunter is correct that no 6-K was filed -- EDGAR shows exactly two 6-Ks in 2026, 2026-03-16 and 2026-06-09 -- and that is the one thing that keeps this below 70, because an ADR holder who reads only filings would not know. Against that: the mechanism does not reach this print. The termination is dated July, so any settlement or royalty charge falls in Q3, and the exclusion-order risk being removed attached to the Helio Ring, a minor SKU inside a $63-68m revenue quarter for which the ITC had issued no remedy and set no target date that would have bitten inside 2026. Removing an unquantified tail on a product line the market has never valued separately is worth low single digits at most, and the 20-day tape is +12.98% through the window in which the ITC notice published.

findings.finding: The share repurchase authorisation that management still describes as active is effectively dormant: Zepp had used US$16.0m of the US$20m program as of 30 June 2025 and only US$17.0m as of 31 March 2026 — about US$1m of buying across nine months during which the ADS fell roughly 90% — leaving US$3m of capacity on a program that expires in November 2026. Shares outstanding are down only 1.66% year over year (14.66m ADS, market cap ~US$72m) against US$103.2m of cash at 31 March 2026.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this 'reconstruction' is printed by the company in its own quarterly press releases, so there is nothing to reconstruct. The cumulative amount used appears each quarter: $16.0m at 2025-06-30, $16.1m at 2025-09-30, $16.2m at 2025-12-31, and $17.0m at 2026-03-31 (the last stated on the Q1 call). The arithmetic also flips the story: because the disclosure is quarterly, ~$0.8m of the ~$1.0m of buying the hunter spreads across nine months in fact occurred inside Q1 2026 alone -- the program was near-frozen through H2 2025 and then accelerated eightfold into the drawdown. 'Effectively dormant' is a defensible read of the nine-month total but a wrong read of the trajectory, and the trajectory is what a marginal holder would care about. On size, the remaining capacity is $3m against a ~$73m market cap and expires November 2026; even full and immediate exhaustion is roughly 4% of cap bought at 38,000 ADS/day, which is a liquidity constraint, not a signal. Shares outstanding down only 1.66% YoY and $103.2m of cash are both disclosed figures in the same documents.

findings.finding: Point72 Asset Management, Point72 Capital Advisors and Steven A. Cohen filed Amendment No. 2 to their Schedule 13G on 14 August 2026 reporting 0.00 shares and 0% of ZEPP as of 30 June 2026 — a full exit. The remaining 13G-scale holder disclosed in the same August window is Morgan Stanley / Morgan Stanley Capital Services at 8.8% with shared voting and dispositive power, i.e. a dealer/swap position rather than a fundamental one.
findings.adversary_note: This is a filing that was headlined by a filings aggregator the day it hit -- StockTitan ran 'Zepp Health holder Point72 reports 0% ownership' on the 2026-08-14 13G/A, and StreetInsider carried the companion Morgan Stanley 13G/A -- so it is wire-level published, not obscure. More decisively, a 13G/A is a backward-looking snapshot: the reported position is 0.00 as of 2026-06-30, meaning the selling was already through a tape averaging ~38,000 ADS a day at some point on or before the end of Q2, and the price has since risen 12.98% over 20 days with no visible adverse reaction to the 14 August filing itself. There is no forward supply left to fear because the position is already zero. The Morgan Stanley 8.8% observation actively weakens the claim rather than strengthening it: shared voting and dispositive power at a broker-dealer with 11,869,344 shares as of 2026-06-30, up from 7.5% at 2025-09-30, is a custody/swap footprint that tells you nothing about fundamental conviction in either direction, and treating it as evidence of an absentee shareholder base is an interpretation, not a fact. A go-to-zero 13G/A on a ~$73m ADR with no analyst coverage is close to information-free.

findings.finding: Cango has published no monthly operational / bitcoin-production update since 2026-06-10 (May data): its own newsroom shows nothing between the 2026-06-24 EGM result and the 2026-08-25 earnings-date notice, so June, July and August updates are all missing -- an 82-day gap against a monthly cadence the company had held since at least mid-2025, and while peer Canaan kept publishing (June update on 2026-07-14). The market's last hashrate/production/treasury data point is therefore 31.67 EH/s, 237.59 BTC and 1,065.11 BTC as of 2026-05-31, and tonight's release supplies the June number nobody has.
findings.adversary_note: The gap is real and I found nobody who has written it down -- but every piece of it is the cheapest possible public observation (the company's own newsroom, and EDGAR showing no 6-K since 2026-07-21), and the innocent explanations are all themselves published: the EGM (2026-06-24), the consolidation ratio/effective-date releases (2026-07-10, 2026-07-21), and management's own statement on the Q1 call that it is 'not setting a hard hashrate target' and is managing to margin rather than scale -- i.e. the company had already told the market it was de-emphasising the exact scale metric the monthly updates carried. Note also the format kept mutating through 2026 ('Bitcoin Production and Mining Operations' -> 'Computing and Energy Operations' -> 'Operational and Fleet Optimization'), which is a company visibly reshaping what it discloses rather than one going silent. Finally the payload is a variance claim, not a directional one -- 'tonight supplies a number nobody has' is true of every earnings release, and the last published data point (31.67 EH/s, 237.59 BTC, 1,065.11 BTC at 5/31) is itself in a 2026-06-10 press release. I concede the pattern-level observation is unpublished; I do not concede it carries a sign.

findings.finding: Antalpha's Q2 2026 report -- filed 2026-08-19, i.e. after Cango last spoke and reporting on the same 30 June balance-sheet date -- states that revenue excluding 'the Cango facility repaid in the first quarter of 2026' was $11.6m, that technology financing fees fell 40% y/y 'primarily reflecting the wind-down of the Cango facility', and that Antalpha has recorded no principal loss since inception. findings.adversary_note: The Antalpha quotes are accurate and I verified them, but the document is a public NASDAQ-company press release from 2026-08-19 indexed on StockTitan and PRNewswire, and the substance was already public from BOTH sides before it: Antalpha said in May that Cango had repaid ~$530m, over 95% of its 12/31/25 balance, and Cango's own 2026-06-01 Q1 release showed long-term debt cut to $30.6m from $557.6m with the $68.2m receivable disclosed on its face. The inferential step the brief actually needs -- that the $68.2m 'releases into unencumbered BTC' -- is asserted, not established: Cango's own disclosure says it funded repayment through bitcoin asset sales, so collateral applied against principal is at least as likely as collateral returned. And the brief does not price the mirror image: BTC fell from $68,233 at 3/31 to ~$58,559 at 6/30, so a receivable marked to BTC takes a further roughly 14% fair-value hit inside the quarter being reported, on top of Q1's $151.8m. I concede that if the release shows a 6/30 treasury materially above the 1,065 BTC last published, that is a real and unconnected surprise against a ~$96m market cap -- which is why this is 58 and not 80.

findings.finding: Yext's own pillar metric went sequentially negative: ARR from customers >=$50K fell from $403.6m at 31 Jan 2026 to $403.1m at 30 Apr 2026 and its YoY growth halved from +2% to +1%, while that cohort's net retention rate dropped 99% -> 97% and total company NRR dropped 97% -> 95% in a single quarter. Straight-line extrapolation puts the >=$50K cohort - 91% of all ARR and the single line management points to as proof of a turn - at zero-to-negative YoY growth in the quarter being reported on 1 Sep.
findings.adversary_note: Every single input to this finding is a number the company itself printed in a shareholder letter, and the second of the two letters is the one that produced a -9.03% reaction. I verified both documents verbatim: the Q4 FY26 letter (2026-03-09) says 'Customers with $50,000 or more of ARR represented $403.6 million or 91% of total ARR' and 'NRR for customers with $50,000 or more of ARR was 99%' / 'NRR was 97% for total customers'; the Q1 FY27 letter (2026-06-02) says 'ARR from customers with annual contract value of $50K or greater was $403.1 million, up 1% year over year', '$50K cohort net retention rate was 97%', 'NRR was 95% for total customers', and 'Total ARR ended the quarter at $440.8 million'. The company does publish the YoY frame rather than the sequential one, so the $403.6m -> $403.1m turn is a derivation -- but it is a one-subtraction derivation between two consecutive letters in the investor-relations tab of a name followed by three analysts, and the broader and more damaging version of the same story (total ARR falling $446.5m -> $444.3m -> $440.8m, sub-$50K ARR -19% YoY, total NRR 95%) was in the wire summary of the June print. The genuinely unpriced part is only the straight-line extrapolation to zero-or-negative YoY in the quarter being reported, and that is a forecast, not a disclosure. It is also the part most likely to be wrong: $403.1m against a $395.3m year-ago base means the cohort can shed $8m sequentially before YoY turns negative, which is a larger step-down than either of the last two quarters produced.

findings.finding: Sell-side revenue estimates have not been cut at all after last quarter's miss: Zacks consensus for Q1 FY27 was ~$111.5m (actual $107.92m, a 3.21% miss) and the consensus now carried into Q2 FY27 is $111.30m - essentially the identical dollar figure - even though the ARR base entering Q2 ($440.8m) is $3.5m lower than the base entering Q1 ($444.3m). The only thing bridging the gap is the extra three days in the May-Jul quarter.
findings.adversary_note: The $111.30m consensus is published -- MarketBeat's own YEXT Q2 FY2027 earnings page carries it alongside $0.17 EPS, and the dailypolitical piece the hunter cites is MarketBeat-syndicated content. But the load-bearing part of the claim is arithmetic, and I think the arithmetic is wrong. The hunter says the only thing bridging $107.92m actual to $111.30m consensus is three extra calendar days. It is not: Q2 FY26 revenue (quarter ended 2025-07-31) was $113.1 million, and Q1 FY26 was $109.5 million, so this company printed a +3.3% Q1-to-Q2 sequential step last year. $107.92m to $111.30m is +3.1% -- the identical seasonal step. Put differently, $111.30m is -1.6% YoY against $113.1m, and Q1 FY27 revenue was -1.4% YoY. The consensus is sitting precisely on the observed YoY decline rate. That is a calibrated estimate, not an uncut one. The claim that estimates 'have not been cut at all' is also contradicted at the analyst-action level: B. Riley Securities downgraded YEXT to Hold and cut its target from $8.00 to $5.00 on 2026-06-03, the day after the miss, and Roth MKM had already cut $9.50 to $6.00 on 2026-03-11. What is left is that a three-analyst blended revenue line has not visibly moved, which on a name with 307 total option contracts of open interest is thin coverage rather than a mispriced bar.

findings.finding: The entire ~50% quarterly rally happened on zero company information: Yext's last substantive press release was 17 Jun 2026 and it made no SEC filing of any kind after 13 Jul 2026 (the 18 Aug release was only the earnings-date notice). findings.adversary_note: This is the tape describing itself, and the sealed baseline already contains it: run_up_20d_pct 20.07, pct_from_52w_low 104.19, pct_from_52w_high -25.55. The news gap is real -- I confirmed the Yext press-release index shows only 2026-06-02 (Q1 results), 2026-06-17 ('Yext Opens Full Platform for Trusted Agentic Marketing Execution') and 2026-08-18 (the earnings-date notice) -- so the factual spine holds. But a rally without news is not information about the print; it is a statement that the marginal buyer's reason is unobservable to us, which is a valuation opinion dressed as a finding. Two of the specific supports are also weak. First, the short-interest direction is cherry-picked: MarketBeat's YEXT short-interest page shows 5.59m shares as of the 2026-08-14 settlement, down from a 16.85m / 14.4%-of-float peak on 2026-03-13. Shorts covered enormously across the rally window; the '+7.64% rise' is one fortnight inside a multi-month collapse in the short base. Second, MarketBeat reports 8.0 days to cover, not 4.63. Third, 'the stock passed both published price targets' is true of B. Riley's $5.00 and the MarketBeat blend, but Needham's Buy and $10.00 target is still on the tape per TipRanks, so the stock has not passed the whole street. Every constituent -- short interest, targets, the $5.75 tender price -- is published on retail-facing pages.

findings.finding: Yext has permanently removed the mechanism behind its only two positive earnings reactions. The Q4 FY26 letter states 'We will no longer provide forward-looking financial guidance' and 'We are suspending quarterly earnings conference calls'; the 18 Aug earnings-date release mentions no call or webcast. Both of the up-prints in the baseline's eight-event history were beat-and-raise / M&A-news events (2025-06-03 +31.5%, 2025-08-18 +8.8%) - a guidance raise is now impossible and there is no Q&A in which management can reframe a weak metric.
