So the finding is factually clean. It is also in the wire copy from the day it happened: TheFly/TipRanks ran 'Yext suspending quarterly guidance' off the 2026-03-09 letter, and it was picked up again in late-March coverage alongside a downgrade. More decisively, the market has now lived through two prints under the new regime -- 2026-03-09 (-2.84%) and 2026-06-02 (-9.03%) -- so no holder is discovering on 1 September that there will be no call and no raise. The analytical overlay ('this removes the mechanism behind the only two up-prints') is a novel framing of known facts, and I do not think it survives its own evidence: the baseline shows 2025-08-18 was a BMO print that went +8.8%, so BMO-plus-no-call is not structurally fatal, and a company that in Q1 FY27 volunteered a GAAP margin range and an EBITDA trajectory has not actually stopped giving forward-looking numbers, whatever the letter says.

findings.finding: A company that says it gives no guidance did quietly set a hard numerical bar for this exact quarter, buried in the 2 Jun shareholder letter: 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%'. Q1 FY27 GAAP net income was only ~2.2% of revenue ($0.02 basic EPS on $107.9m), so hitting the low end of its own range in Q2 requires GAAP net income of roughly $11-17m - a 4-7x sequential jump - against a rising interest bill on $150m of newly drawn term debt.
findings.adversary_note: The quotes are real -- the Q1 FY27 letter says 'we expect...GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%' -- but 'buried' is not defensible. Both sentences appear in the outlook section of the letter and both were lifted into third-party wire summaries of the 2026-06-02 8-K on the day (StockTitan's write-up carries 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range' and 'quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%' as quoted management outlook). It has been public and quotable for 91 days. The arithmetic gap is the part with residual value, and I think the hunter overstates it. Q1 FY27 had Adjusted EBITDA of $26.9m at a 25% margin against GAAP net income of $2.6m -- a $24.3m gap that is mostly SBC, amortisation and interest. Push EBITDA to ~30% of ~$111m, i.e. ~$33m, hold the gap constant, and GAAP net income lands near $9m, or ~8% -- a modest shortfall against a 10% low end, not a company that needs a miracle. And the headline the tape will trade is non-GAAP EPS against $0.17 (MarketBeat) or $0.10 (Zacks) versus $0.15 basic / $0.14 diluted last quarter; a GAAP-margin shortfall against a self-set 'expectation' is a second-order line item on a name with no call, no Q&A and three analysts.

findings.finding: The offsetting positive tail: $114.9m of repurchase authorization was live for the whole of Q2 FY27 with ZERO open-market buybacks used as of 30 Apr 2026 ($14.9m remaining plus $100.0m added by the board in May 2026, disclosed as a subsequent event), while the stock traded between the $3.27 52-week low and ~$5.75 for most of May-July. Two directors bought personally in the same window - Seth Waugh 133,000 shares at $3.746 on 11 Jun and Daniel Englander 76,190 shares at $5.2226 on 13 Jul - and the CEO had bid $9.00/share for the company in 2025. The 1 Sep 10-Q is the first disclosure of whether the company bought, and shares outstanding were still 100,248,116 as of 19 May.
findings.adversary_note: The authorisation arithmetic verifies against the 10-Q -- $14.9m remaining at 2026-04-30, an additional $100.0m authorised by the board in May 2026 as a subsequent event, and 'During the quarter ended April 30, 2026, no repurchases were made under the share repurchase program' -- and the $100m expansion was itself the wire headline on 2026-06-02 (StockTitan: 'Yext posts Q1 FY27 profit and expands $100M share buyback'). The Form 4s are public on filing: EDGAR shows insider filings on 2026-06-12 and 2026-07-13 matching the Waugh and Englander purchases, and the CEO's $9.00 bid was widely reported in 2025. So the entire ex-ante fact set is published. The one genuinely new datum is whether they bought in Q2, and that is a known-unknown of ambiguous sign rather than information. I also think the sign reasoning here is backwards. The reason there were no open-market repurchases in the April quarter is that the company was busy repurchasing 24.3 million shares for $140 million at $5.75 in a modified Dutch auction that closed 2026-03-18, funded by drawing $150m of a $200m BlackRock facility. Management did not decline to buy its own stock; it just spent $140m and most of its debt capacity doing it. That makes an aggressive Q2 open-market program less likely, not more, and it means the $114.9m headroom is closer to a paper authorisation than a coiled bid -- especially with the stock trading well above the $5.75 the company was willing to pay.

findings.finding: Rezolve has issued no new shares since the January 2026 raise (398.83m shares outstanding today = 336,327,587 at 31 Dec 2025 + the 62,500,000 sold at $4.00 on 21 Jan 2026, to the share), which lets H1 cash be bounded from the outside: $111.1m at 31 Dec 2025 + $250m gross January proceeds - $230m paid all-cash for Reward Loyalty on 10 Feb 2026 = at most ~$131m before H1 operating burn (FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was -$59m) and before the ~$102m Crownpeak/Monroe term loan that matures 31 Dec 2026 - so only a small single-digit-percent fraction of the $300m repurchase mandate is actually fundable, and the H1 balance sheet is where that arithmetic first becomes public.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this arithmetic is published and at least one retail-facing outlet has already run the same subtraction. The 20-F (2026-03-30) discloses cash of $111,112,251, a $87.1m working capital deficit, $102.1m of SHORT-TERM borrowings, $50.1m long-term, and -- far harsher than anything the claim concludes -- an explicit 'substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.' The January raise (62.5m shares at $4.00, closed 2026-01-21) and the $230m all-cash Reward payment (2026-02-10) were both wire events. merlintrader's RZLV hub already states the net position is 'broadly in the same region as where it started' and that no repurchase had been announced as of 2026-08-04. A market that has been told 'going concern doubt' does not need to be told 'the $300m buyback is only single-digit-percent fundable' -- the stronger fact is out and the stock is 63% below its 52w high. Separately, the load-bearing premise is weaker than presented: 398,827,587 is the count stockanalysis carries, which is plausibly the 20-F cover-page figure struck after the January close, so it does NOT establish zero issuance February-August 2026 -- particularly with the going-concern paragraph naming an active ATM program as a mitigation. The genuinely new datum is the actual 30-Jun-2026 cash number, and that is one line of the print, not an unpriced insight.

findings.finding: The UK statutory accounts of Rezolve AI PLC (company 14573691) for the year ended 31 December 2025 were due at Companies House by 30 June 2026 and are still not filed as of 31 August 2026 - the register shows the last accounts on file as the period ending 31 December 2024 and flags accounts overdue - even though the company published an 'Annual Report and Accounts 2025' as Exhibit 99.2 to a 6-K on 30 March 2026, and its shareholders only passed the resolution covering auditor appointment on a resolution filed 22 July 2026, three weeks after the statutory deadline.
findings.adversary_note: I concede the publication test: I searched and found no market-facing coverage of the plc's Companies House delinquency, and I independently verified the register does show 'Accounts overdue' with last accounts made up to 31 December 2024 against a 30 June 2026 due date. The marginal RZLV holder is a US retail/momentum holder reading GlobeNewswire, not the UK register, so this is genuinely obscure. But it is obscure and small in the same breath: the company filed a 20-F on time on 2026-03-30 with audited FY2025 statements and furnished the Annual Report as a 6-K exhibit, so the information content of the UK statutory filing is nil -- this is a compliance-calendar failure, not a withheld number. There is also no mechanism into the 09-01 print: the 6-K will not mention Companies House and the interims are unaudited by construction. One sub-claim is wrong: resolutions filed at the register on 22 July 2026 almost certainly record the AGM held 30 June 2026 (the same meeting that carried the buyback mandate), so the auditor resolution was passed ON the statutory deadline, not 'three weeks after' it -- the hunter has read a filing date as a passing date.

findings.finding: Rezolve AI PLC - the listed parent itself, not a US subsidiary - registered a charge in favour of Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC created 22 December 2025 and still outstanding, plus a second outstanding charge in favour of Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC created 19 January 2026, meaning the ~$102m of Crownpeak term loans maturing 31 December 2026 (Term SOFR + 5.50%) are secured at the top of the group; the $300m buyback in turn requires a UK court-sanctioned capital reduction, expected mid-September, in which secured creditors get a formal creditor-protection say.
findings.adversary_note: Split the claim. The debt facts are fully published: the 20-F carries $102.1m as short-term borrowings and $50.1m long-term, and stocktitan headlined the filing 'Rezolve AI 20-F details losses and going-concern risk' on 2026-03-30. The mid-September court timetable for the capital reduction is in the company's own 2026-06-30 release. What is not published anywhere I can find is that the charges sit on the LISTED PARENT rather than a US subsidiary, and the inference that secured creditors get formal creditor protection in a s.641 court-sanctioned reduction -- that is a real, non-obvious channel by which the buyback could slip, and it is the part I score low. Two things cap the number. First, the mechanism resolves at a mid-September hearing, not at the 09-01 print, so it reaches this event only if management addresses it on the call. Second, the claim mis-assigns the lenders: it calls the $102m 'Crownpeak/Monroe term loans', whereas the 20-F and this brief's own RZLV-h2#2 put $101,540,086 with Monroe (short-term) and $50,000,000 with Crownpeak (promissory notes). Crownpeak Technology Holdings is the acquisition seller, and seller-note creditors routinely consent as part of a negotiated deal, which materially softens the creditor-veto story.

findings.finding: Rezolve took a $63.3m impairment in FY2025 on its SQD (Subsquid) token holdings and told investors continued volatility could force further impairments; SQD traded around a $0.0627 low in January 2026 and was capped by a $0.056-$0.058 resistance zone by June 2026, so the H1 2026 accounts most likely carry another digital-asset writedown into a net loss line the market has no estimate for, because only the revenue line was pre-announced.
findings.adversary_note: This is the finding whose own numbers refute its materiality. The $63,345,577 FY2025 impairment is a named line in the 20-F income statement and was summarised by stocktitan on 2026-03-30, and the 'continued volatility could force further impairments' warning is the company's own published risk factor -- so the existence of the risk is out. The magnitude is bounded and trivial: total digital assets on the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet are only ~$16.4m ('other digital assets') plus ~$0.1m crypto intangibles, and Rezolve's stated policy is to add SQD equal to roughly 1% of revenue (~$1.3m a half). The claim's own price path -- $0.0627 in January to a $0.056-0.058 zone by June -- is a ~10-14% decline, i.e. roughly $2m of writedown against a $1.14bn market cap, or 0.2%. Even a total write-off of the whole $16.4m is 1.4% of cap and lands in a non-cash line inside a company that already printed a $101.4m net loss. The 'no consensus on the net loss line' observation is true but this name trades on the revenue/ARR narrative and five analysts carry a $10.50 target; nobody is marking it on the impairment line.

findings.finding: Reward Loyalty UK Limited (CH 10701520), the business Rezolve bought for $239,557,869 cash on 2026-02-10 and told US investors would add 'approximately $90 million of EBITDA-accretive revenue', filed audited group accounts at Companies House on 2026-07-25 for its year ended 30 April 2025 showing turnover of GBP 52.89m (approx $67-71m) and gross profit of about GBP 21m - i.e. a ~40% gross-margin business generating roughly GBP 2m EBITDA on 186-209 employees, not a 90%-margin software asset. [snippet_only: the 74-page PDF is behind an S3 redirect WebFetch cannot follow; figures are from two independent CH aggregators reading the same filing]
findings.adversary_note: The strongest of the eight, and I only partly resist it. I verified the filing exists: Companies House shows group accounts for Reward Loyalty UK Limited (10701520) year ended 30 April 2025, filed 25 July 2026, 74 pages. I found no market-facing coverage of its contents, and the gross-margin (~40%) and ~GBP2m EBITDA detail is genuinely unpublished. Three things stop this being a 10. First, the order-of-magnitude gap was already checkable before the deal: aggregators carry ~GBP53m turnover for Reward's YE 30 April 2024 accounts, filed 31 January 2025 -- thirteen months before Rezolve told investors the asset added 'approximately $90 million of EBITDA-accretive revenue.' Anyone who pulled the register in February 2026 saw the same gap. Second, the frame has circulated: Fuzzy Panda's report of 2025-09-29 is explicitly 'Faking ARR by Acquiring Failing AI Start-ups w/ Declining Revenue', which is this exact allegation applied to this exact strategy, and the stock fell on it. Third, the number is disclosed by the event itself -- the 09-01 interims consolidate Reward from 10 February and will show the blended gross margin, so this is less 'unpriced fact' than 'correct prediction of a line item hours away'. findings.finding: Rezolve's consolidated gross margin has already fallen from the 95.8% it reported for H1 2025 to 66.0% for audited FY2025 (revenue $46,800,099 less cost of revenue $15,922,202 per the 20-F income statement), which implies roughly 61% in H2 2025 - and H1 2026 is the FIRST period that consolidates Reward at all, on top of Crownpeak (from 1 Dec 2025) and GroupBy. The 1 September interims are the first gross-margin disclosure the market will see since the 95.8% print.
findings.adversary_note: The gross-margin collapse from 95.8% to 66.0% is not a discovery -- it is two published numbers, and I reproduced the second directly from the 20-F XBRL: revenue $46,800,099 less cost of revenue $15,922,202 equals $30,877,897, exactly 66.0%. That filing is five months old, and merlintrader's public RZLV hub already prints 'audited FY2025 gross margin was 66.0% on revenue of $46.8 million.' What is not written down anywhere is the implied ~61% H2 2025 exit rate, and the forward step-down from consolidating a ~40%-margin Reward on top of Crownpeak and GroupBy -- that is the live content, and it rests on the same Companies House PDF as RZLV-h2#0, so the two findings are one bet, not two. The counterweight is that this is a pure guess about a line item the print will disclose in a few hours; the market's problem with RZLV has never been gross margin, it has been whether the revenue is real. A company that can hold 60% while 20x-ing revenue would be read bullishly by the same holders who bid the stock 22% on a press release with no contract value.

findings.finding: Both of Rezolve AI PLC's registered charges are still shown as OUTSTANDING at Companies House - Monroe Capital Management Advisors LLC (charge created 2025-12-22) and Crownpeak Technology Holdings LLC (created 2026-01-19) - covering the $101,540,086 Monroe borrowing that the 20-F classified as SHORT-TERM debt at 31 Dec 2025 and the $50,000,000 Crownpeak promissory notes, while no 6-K filed in 2026 announces any refinancing, and the 20-F's going-concern mitigation depended explicitly on 'refinancing short-term debt'. Cash arithmetic: $111,112,251 at 31 Dec 2025, plus the ~$250m registered direct raise closed 2026-01-21 (62.5m shares at $4, ~5% placement fee), less the $239,557,869 cash paid for Reward on 2026-02-10, leaves roughly $110m before any H1 operating burn (FY2025 operating burn was $63,147,255 on a far smaller cost base). The 1 September interims are the first balance sheet since 31 Dec 2025.
findings.adversary_note: This is RZLV-h1#0 and RZLV-h1#2 restated with more decimal places, and the decimals are all from the 20-F. $111,112,251 cash, $101,540,086 Monroe classified short-term, $50,000,000 Crownpeak notes, the $63,147,255 operating burn and the going-concern mitigation resting on 'refinancing short-term debt' are every one of them in a filing published 2026-03-30 and summarised in a stocktitan headline the same day. The $250m raise and the $239,557,869 Reward payment were wire events in January and February. The residual ~$110m is already in print on merlintrader's hub. The only genuinely new observations are (a) the charges remain OUTSTANDING on the UK register and (b) no 6-K in 2026 announces a refinancing -- the second of which is an absence any EDGAR reader can see for free, and the first of which tells you nothing about whether a refinancing is in negotiation. A market told 'substantial doubt about going concern' in March has already been given the worst version of this claim; the incremental information on 09-01 is the actual 30-June cash figure, and the sign of the surprise is not knowable from the register.

findings.finding: The entire +16.8% five-day run-up in the baseline is one company-issued press release: 'Google Selects Rezolve Ai's Proprietary Distributed Database Platform' on 2026-08-25, which moved the stock ~19% in a session (close 2.43 on 08-24, pre-market 2.645 on 08-25) and which discloses no contract value, no term, no revenue and no Google quote or spokesperson; Google's own Blockchain Analytics / Web3 documentation and partner blogs name Subsquid and Chainstack for exactly this function and do not mention Rezolve; and Rezolve did not furnish the release on a Form 6-K, its last 6-K being 2026-08-06.
findings.adversary_note: The first half of this is priced by identity, not by argument: the run-up attribution is arithmetically exact -- 2.8375 divided by the 2.43 close of 08-24 is 1.1677, precisely the baseline's +16.77% five-day figure -- and the 08-25 release moved the stock roughly +22% intraday on the day it was published on GlobeNewswire and covered by Yahoo, Manila Times, Kalkine, martechseries and stocktitan. A price move caused by a document everyone read is the definition of in the price. The 'no contract value, no term, no Google quote' observation is visible on the face of that same press release, and the paid-partnership frame was published by Fuzzy Panda on 2025-09-29 ('partnerships with Microsoft and Google are not true collaborations but arrangements where Rezolve pays the tech giants'), so the skepticism has already circulated and been traded. And the claim's central piece of corroborating evidence is self-defeating: Rezolve ACQUIRED Subsquid on 2025-10-09, so Google Cloud Web3 documentation naming Subsquid for exactly this indexing function is confirmation that Rezolve's technology is in the stack, not evidence against it. That is the one factual error in this brief that I would call load-bearing.

findings.finding: The reaffirmed ~$360m FY2026 guide requires H2 2026 revenue of ~$233m against ~$127m in H1, +83% half-on-half, at a point where the acquired run-rates are largely already in the base: Reward at GBP 52.89m/yr (~$67-71m), Crownpeak at ~$70m/yr for an $81.0m purchase price, GroupBy at ~$30m/yr - about $84m per half combined - leaving roughly $149m of H2 from everything else versus roughly $43m in H1.
findings.adversary_note: The headline arithmetic is a subtraction anyone can do and somebody already has: $360m minus $127m is $233m, and merlintrader's public hub states 'roughly $233 million in second-half revenue -- approximately 1.8 times the preliminary first-half figure of $127 million.' Both inputs were wire copy (2026-07-27 preliminary H1, guidance reaffirmed 2026-07-27 and again 2026-08-06 alongside the 09-01 call notice). The additive content is the acquired-run-rate decomposition, and it rests on the same Reward Loyalty PDF as RZLV-h2#0 -- same document, same bet. It also has a soft spot: Reward consolidated only from 10 February, so H1 carried roughly 4.7 of 6 months of it, which means the acquired base in H1 is nearer $75m than $84m and the residual is nearer $50m than $43m; and H2 mechanically picks up the missing Reward stub plus a full half of anything closed mid-year, which is part of how the company gets to a $500m exit ARR claim. The bear case here is 'the guide is a stretch', which is exactly what a stock 63% below its 52-week high on 86% realised vol with a Fuzzy Panda report on file already says.
